current_engineering_outputs.body: Evidence E1–E3, E26, E37, E39 and E61–E63 supports separate control and content responsibilities. Place retrieval, document parsing and the open-weight runtime inside the customer tenant. Attach source ACLs to chunks, retrieval and answers. Keep customer keys and runtime plaintext outside provider administrative access. At-rest encryption alone cannot prove that boundary during inference. Exclude payloads from consoles, OOB recordings, dumps, traces, support bundles and snapshots. Emit only explicitly classified infrastructure facts to the provider. The provider copilot uses its own manuals and those facts. It returns diagnostic steps that the customer administrator executes inside the content boundary. For C3, bind the actual subscription and support scope. For SAI, use the verified End Customer resale route or an effective direct-use variation. A narrower reseller-administration design needs its own evidenced resale purpose. Resolve model licences, integration terms and the elected site before deployment. current_engineering_outputs.body: Evidence E27, E36–E40, E45, E52, E55 and E62–E63 separates hardware support from content interpretation. Reject unknown producers, arbitrary log bodies, command output, memory dumps and mixed records. Reject customer snippets, prompt fields and filenames with content. Check confidentiality and Personal Data separately. Exclusion from Customer Data does not erase either duty. Return a provider-runbook reference, fault classification and a customer-executable diagnostic step. The customer retains any content-rich result. Do not treat a redacted workload as non-content without an actual content and reconstruction test. This alternative does not activate D2 or D5, which specifically require provider access to customer content.

current_engineering_outputs.body: C3 base agreement: platform, distribution, noncompetition and preferred-platform clauses establish actors and scope, not a universal data licence. Sections 8 and 9 preserve ownership, qualifying contributions, use limits, recipient designations, return and survival. The internal MSSA and downstream subscriptions remain independent sources. SAI: preserve definitions, resale scope, monitoring proviso, keys, residency, Personal Data roles, IP, feedback, confidentiality, AUP and actual service readiness. Section 15.4 is the strongest specific improvement override. Its qualifying feedback and Background IPR boundary must survive the raw-workload refusal. Section 15.5 requires actual incorporation. Open-source rights concern the component, not service purpose or customer data. The broad Foreground IPR definition does not eliminate 15.2's application-layer exclusion or establish access authority. AUP compliance investigations, compelled disclosure and audit have distinct scopes. Audit expressly excludes Customer Data. AUP changes, SLA changes and infrastructure maintenance have their own notice mechanisms. None is a generic AI launch-notice route. Backup security language creates no dedicated customer-backup service or permission for out-of-site copies. The included order supplies hardware-only support, customer-managed application/storage responsibilities, integration conditions and shared OOB risk. Security, KYC, financing, pledge, tax, termination, indemnity, insurance and dispute terms remain relevant to their subjects. They do not grant a new AI content purpose or prove payment, signatures, commissioning, current contract status or supplier engagement. Redacted financial and account fields remain redacted. The separate pledge purpose creates no feature data-access right. Fullstory is shared source context, not a third customer or an incorporated amendment. Its historical version proves only its captured disclosure. Exact quote verification proves provenance. It cannot prove legal correctness or current customer clearance.
